{"path":"snake_openrouter-moonshotai-kimi-k3_01.html","edit_description":"Create a NEW complete single-file HTML5 Snake game. All CSS and JavaScript must be inline in this one file — no external resources, no CDN links. The file must be fully self-contained and runnable by double-clicking it.

== CORE GAME ==
- 30x30 grid rendered on a <canvas> (600x600 px, 20px cells), dark retro theme with subtle grid lines.
- Two snakes always play simultaneously (every mode is a versus mode). Snake 1 = green, Snake 2 = orange.
- Snakes move continuously via a fixed-tick game loop (~110ms per tick, setInterval or requestAnimationFrame accumulator), in one of 4 directions. A snake cannot reverse 180°. Use a direction queue so rapid key presses within one tick cannot cause an illegal reversal.
- Food (red apple) spawns at a random empty cell never occupied by either snake. Eating food grows that snake by 1 segment and increments its score by 1. Keep exactly one food on the board at all times.
- Collision rules: hitting a wall, its own body, or the other snake's body/head kills that snake. When a snake dies the game ends and the survivor wins. If both snakes die on the same tick (head-on collision), the result is a draw.

== CONTROLS ==
- Player 1 (green): WASD keys. Player 2 (orange): Arrow keys.
- In "CPU vs Human" mode the single human player controls their snake with BOTH WASD and arrow keys.
- preventDefault on arrow keys and space so the page does not scroll.
- Start menu: pressing 1 = Human vs Human, 2 = CPU vs Human, 3 = CPU vs CPU (buttons also clickable).
- Game over screen: pressing R (also Enter or Space) instantly restarts the same mode; pressing M or Escape returns to the start menu.

== CPU AI ==
- CPU snakes automatically search for food using BFS (breadth-first search) shortest path from head to food on the 30x30 grid, treating both snakes' bodies as obstacles (tail cells that will move may be treated as free).
- If a safe path to food exists, follow its first step.
- Fallback survival behavior: if no path to food exists, evaluate each non-lethal neighbor move with a flood-fill count of reachable open cells and pick the move with the largest reachable area. If every move is lethal, keep moving straight.
- In "CPU vs CPU" mode both snakes use this AI.

== UI / SCREENS ==
Implement a clean state machine with three states: MENU, PLAYING, GAME_OVER. Use HTML overlays (divs) over the canvas for menu and game-over screens.
- Start menu overlay: big title "SNAKE", three mode buttons ("Human vs Human", "CPU vs Human", "CPU vs CPU"), a controls legend (P1: WASD, P2: Arrows, R: restart), hint "Press 1 / 2 / 3 or click".
- HUD during gameplay (always visible above or overlaid on the canvas): current mode label and live scores, e.g. "Green: 3   |   CPU vs Human   |   Orange: 5". Update scores immediately when food is eaten.
- Game over overlay: winner text ("Green Wins!", "Orange Wins!" or "Draw!"), final scores for both snakes, and "Press R to restart — M for menu".
- Retro styling: dark background (#0a0a12 or similar), neon green/orange snakes with slightly glowing heads, rounded body cells, monospace/pixel-style font (system monospace stack is fine), centered layout.

== STRUCTURE & QUALITY ==
- Single HTML file: <!DOCTYPE html>, <head> with <meta charset> and <style>, <body> containing the canvas, HUD, and overlay divs, then one <script> block at the end of body.
- All code and comments in English. Keep it organized: constants at top, game state object, input handling, AI functions (bfsPath, floodFillCount, cpuChooseMove), update/step logic, render functions, screen/state management.
- Ensure correctness: the game loop must be properly started/stopped when switching screens; restarting must fully reset snake positions (e.g. green starts left side heading right, orange starts right side heading left), scores, food, and direction queues; food spawn must never overlap a snake; simultaneous-eat and head-on edge cases handled sensibly.
- The file must be complete and immediately playable with no console errors."}
